notes: Refined front-center sensor position forward to y=0.065 m to improve forward line sensing and anticipation of curvature, maintaining sensor size and wheel track for stability. Controller PID gains slightly adjusted for smooth control with the refined sensor layout. Observation request includes steering oscillation to monitor control smoothness.
rationale: The previous iteration's geometry with larger sensors (0.016 m), an added front-center sensor at y=0.06 m, and a wider wheel track (0.14 m) showed excellent performance on both the oval and s-bend tracks, with zero line loss events and low steering oscillation. The telemetry confirms stable line detection and smooth control, with no line loss and near-complete progress on both tracks. Given this strong performance, I maintain the sensor size at 0.016 m and the wheel track at 0.14 m to preserve stability and line detection quality. I propose a slight refinement in sensor positions to optimize forward sensing and lateral coverage: reposition the front-center sensor slightly forward to y=0.065 m to better anticipate line curvature, and adjust lateral sensors to maintain balanced coverage. The body dimensions, wheel radius, and mass remain unchanged to keep the robot's dynamics consistent. The controller is tuned with PID gains to balance responsiveness and smoothness, with sensor weights adjusted to leverage the refined sensor layout. I request measurements including steering_oscillation, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, completion, and progress to verify stability and line following robustness on all tracks.
